entities.summary: Chancellor of the Pharaoh Djoser, architect of the Step Pyramid at Saqqara (the world's first monumental stone structure, c. 2670 BCE), and one of the earliest known physicians. Imhotep was a rare commoner who achieved near-divine status — later deified as a god of medicine and wisdom (equated with Greek Asclepius). He is credited with pioneering stone architecture and possibly authoring the earliest medical and wisdom texts. His reputation persisted for over 2,000 years after his death, making him one of the most enduring intellectual figures of the ancient world.
